rationale: C23 is a highly plausible direct drafting template. It uses the same two-recital structure: identification of a labor dispute followed by a presidential finding that it threatens a strike or lockout affecting a substantial part of an interstate industry and imperiling national health and safety. Its operative provisions then match the child nearly verbatim, including the Board's Title II powers, a section 206 reporting deadline, and continued existence after the report. C13 and C24 share essentially the same machinery, but C23 is the closest and most recent displayed predecessor.

shared_material.child_excerpt: WHEREAS in my opinion such disputes threaten to result in strikes or lockouts affecting a substantial part of the maritime industry ... which strikes or lockouts, if permitted to occur, will imperil the national health and safety
shared_material.parent_excerpt: WHEREAS in my opinion such dispute threatens to result in a strike or lock-out affecting a substantial part of the communications industry ... which strike or lock-out, if permitted to occur, will imperil the national health and safety
shared_material.explanation: Distinctive language and syntax are preserved while the affected industry and factual parties are changed.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The Board shall have powers and duties as set forth in Title II of the said Act. The Board shall report to the President in accordance with the provisions of section 206 of the said Act on or before June 11, 1948.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Board shall have powers and duties as set forth in Title II of the said Act. The Board shall report to the President in accordance with the provisions of section 206 of the said Act on or before June 8, 1948.
shared_material.explanation: The central administrative machinery is virtually identical, with only the reporting date changed.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Upon the submission of its report, the Board shall continue in existence to perform such other functions as may be required under the said Act, until the Board is terminated by the President.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Upon the submission if its report, the Board shall continue in existence to perform such other functions as may be required under the said Act, until the Board is terminated by the President.
shared_material.explanation: The post-report continuation and presidential-termination clause is reproduced nearly verbatim.
